slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated particles
slot.brief: Find the de Broglie wavelength of an electron (or alpha particle) accelerated through a given potential difference using λ = h/√(2meV).

stem: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of $150$ V. Find its de Broglie wavelength. Take $h=6.63\times10^{-34}$ J s, $m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}$ kg and $e=1.60\times10^{-19}$ C.
solution:
The electron gains kinetic energy $eV$, so its momentum is $p=\sqrt{2m_e eV}$ and its de Broglie wavelength is
$$\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2m_e eV}}=\frac{6.63\times10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2(9.11\times10^{-31})(1.60\times10^{-19})(150)}}\approx1.00\times10^{-10}\,\text{m}.$$
